hypotheses.binder: (hw : ∀ n x, x ∈ s.domain → 0 ≤ w n x)
hypotheses.justification: The only role of `hw` in the proof is `LocalJets.bilinear` (via `bilinear_jet_at` / `majorant_nonneg`), where it is used at a single point `(n, x)` with `x ∈ s.domain`, `x ∈ K n i` to show `0 ≤ majorant s w α A p n x`. Now `majorant s w α C p n x = C * s.epsilon n ^ α * s.growth n x ^ p * w n x` (`WeightedClasses.majorant`), where `s.epsilon n ^ α > 0` (`Real.rpow_pos_of_pos`, `s.epsilon_pos`) and `s.growth n x ^ p ≥ 1 > 0` (`StripData.one_le_growth`). So the sign of the majorant (for `C > 0`) is the sign of `w n x`. Case 1: there are `n i x` with `x ∈ s.domain`, `x ∈ K n i`, `w n x < 0`. Then for every `m` the constant `C` supplied by `hf.bounds m` must be `0`: at `j = 0` the bound reads `0 ≤ ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 (f n i) x‖ ≤ C * (positive) * w n x < 0` if `C > 0` (use `norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero`). Hence all jets `iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (f n i) x` with `j ≤ m` vanish at every point of `s.domain ∩ K n i`, and so do all jets of `x ↦ f n i x * g n i x` up to order `m` (the Leibniz sum only involves jets of `f` of order `≤ m`, and `hg.smooth` gives all jets of `g`). Thus the conclusion holds with constant `C = 0`, since `majorant s (w·v) (α+β) 0 p n x = 0`. Case 2: `0 ≤ w n x` for all `n, x` with `x ∈ s.domain ∩ K n i`. Then the call `hf.bilinear hg (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ)` only needs `0 ≤ w n x` at the points of the cells where the majorant is evaluated, which is exactly the available information; `hv` is still a valid argument of `bilinear`, so the original proof goes through verbatim (or one applies `bilinear_jet_at` directly with the pointwise-nonnegative majorants). So `hw` can be deleted (and also deleted together with `hv`).

hypotheses.binder: (hv : ∀ n x, x ∈ s.domain → 0 ≤ v n x)
hypotheses.justification: Symmetric to `hw`. `hv` is consumed only through `majorant_nonneg s v β B q n x` inside `LocalJets.bilinear`/`bilinear_jet_at`. Since `majorant s v β B q n x = B * s.epsilon n ^ β * s.growth n x ^ q * v n x` with `s.epsilon n ^ β > 0` and `s.growth n x ^ q ≥ 1`, the majorant is negative exactly where `B > 0` and `v n x < 0`. If some `n i x` with `x ∈ s.domain`, `x ∈ K n i` has `v n x < 0`, then the constant of `hg.bounds m` is forced to be `0` (bound at `j = 0`, using `norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero`), so all jets of `g n i` up to order `m` vanish on `s.domain ∩ K n i` and therefore all jets of `f n i * g n i` up to order `m` vanish there; the conclusion then holds with constant `C = 0` because `majorant` with constant `0` is identically `0`. Otherwise `0 ≤ v n x` on `s.domain ∩ K n i`, which is all that `bilinear`/`bilinear_jet_at` needs (the hypothesis enters only at the bound's point `(n,x)`), and the original proof applies unchanged with `hw` as given. Hence `hv` is deletable on its own, and also simultaneously with `hw`: the three-case split `w < 0` somewhere in a cell / `v < 0` somewhere in a cell / both nonnegative on cells covers every situation, so `LocalJets s (fun n x => w n x * v n x) (α + β) K (fun n i x => f n i x * g n i x)` is provable from `hf` and `hg` alone.
